# Synthetic sshd dataset (labelled, reproducible)

**Synthetic.** Every record here is generated by `backend/app/evaluation/synthetic.py`
from seed `20261115`; no log line comes from a real system. Addresses are drawn
from `198.18.0.0/15` (RFC 2544 benchmarking), one pool for every role, so an
address range never reveals a label.

The full datasets are not committed because they do not need to be: the
generator rebuilds them in seconds, byte for byte. What is committed is what a
reader needs to check that claim and to see what the data looks like.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `manifest-1d.json`, `manifest-7d.json` | Seed, generator version, counts and the SHA-256 of every generated file |
| `episodes-7d.json` | The 60 injected attack campaigns of the 7-day evaluation set (12 per scenario) |
| `excerpt-events.jsonl` | 182 raw sshd messages around one brute-force campaign, as the parser sees them |
| `excerpt-labels.jsonl` | The ground truth for those records, kept in a separate file |

Rebuild and verify:

```bash
make dataset     # writes runtime-data/eval/synthetic-{1d,7d}/ and checks both manifests
```

## Ground truth

An *episode* is a campaign from the scenario catalogue: brute force that
succeeds, password spray, low-and-slow guessing, a spray distributed over many
addresses, and credential stuffing that ends in a login. Opportunistic internet
scanning against generic usernames that never succeeds is background noise and
is labelled `benign`, as are users mistyping passwords, automation, and a
monitor retrying an expired password.

Two scenarios are shaped to sit near or below the per-source rule thresholds.
On the 7-day set the rules raise at least one alert for 42 of the 60 episodes
(distributed spray 1/12, low-and-slow 5/12, the other three 12/12), so the rule
layer alone already caps recall; that is reported, not hidden, in
[EVALUATION.md](../../EVALUATION.md).
